tasks.title: Make evidence revocation and restoration safe and replay-consistent
tasks.description: In orchestrator/creator_dna/store.py, separate creator rejection from attribution revocation. Today revoke_attribution() and reject_evidence() both write evidence_review/reject, _apply() treats every action other than reject as a restore, and restore_evidence() can make evidence from a withdrawn attribution eligible again (also after replay); a revocation of already creator-rejected evidence is not recorded at all. Fix: independent creator_rejected and attribution_revoked state with rejected kept as a read-only compatibility property; a distinct attribution_revoked event (decision ID and reason, schema v4); strict evidence_review actions (reject, restore only); restore clears only creator rejection and is refused for revoked or flagged possible-legacy-revoked evidence; revocation is recorded even for creator-rejected evidence and is idempotent per decision. Legacy v1-v3 logs replay with their original semantics; a note-prefix heuristic may only set read-only warning flags. Synthetic regression tests and a documentation update. No change to speaker_attribution/ or any cross-package test; no real footage.
acceptance_criteria: Creator rejection and attribution revocation are independent state; EvidenceItem.rejected stays a read-only property true for either, and existing readers of rejected and review_note are unchanged
Revocation is written as a distinct attribution_revoked event with decision ID and reason (schema v4); evidence_review accepts only reject and restore and any other action fails replay
restore_evidence clears only creator rejection, never undoes a current revocation, and is refused for revoked evidence and for evidence flagged as a possible legacy revocation
revoke_attribution records a revocation for creator-rejected evidence; repeated revoke_attribution/sync_revocations for the same decision emit no new events
Legacy v1-v3 logs replay with original semantics; ambiguous historical rejects are only flagged (read-only warnings), never migrated or reinterpreted
Exports keep rejected_by_creator creator-specific and expose attribution revocation, decision ID and reason separately

Synthetic regression tests cover revoke then restore, creator reject then revoke, unknown actions, reload/replay equivalence, repeated synchronization and legacy replay/reporting; test_speaker_attribution.py passes unmodified

tasks.description: Wave w04-autonomy-loop, lane L1: Autonomy loop: task selection, wake-up wait and Main Stop hook (issue #44, mission part 2-4).
acceptance_criteria: New module orchestrator/dev_supervisor/autonomy.py with its own CLI `python -B -m dev_supervisor.autonomy <cmd>` (do NOT edit cli.py, launch.py, telemetry.py or any other existing module: they are claimed by open tasks T-DEV-010..012); standard library only; reuse existing modules read-only (state_store.StateStore, workers.WorkerRegistry, config.Config loading as cli.py does, evidence labels)

`next [--json] [--repo <root>]`: builds the actionable list for Main from the repository records and the supervisor state, ordered by priority with a reason each: (a) worker results that are REPORTED and not yet verified (review_worker_result); (b) FAILED or LOST workers and whether a retry is eligible or blocked (bounded restarts, identical-failure stop); (c) wave lanes SUBMITTED but not verified, read from waves/*/wave.json plus `git` remote branch state via an injected runner; (d) registered tasks in ACTIVE_TASKS.json / DEVELOPMENT_TRACKER.json that are eligible: PLANNED or the next PLANNED step of an ACTIVE task whose dependencies are COMPLETED and whose owned_paths do not overlap another ACTIVE task; (e) blocked items with the exact blocker (dependency, lease held by another task, missing merge). When nothing is actionable it returns an explicit idle_reason (for example 'waiting for 2 running workers' or 'no eligible task: T-X waits for T-Y'). Never invents work; repository files win over supervisor cache

`wait --timeout <s> [--poll <s>] [--cursor <file>]`: blocks until the actionable fingerprint changes or a new supervisor event (events.jsonl beyond a stored cursor) of kind worker_* / main_* / replacement arrives, prints a short JSON summary of what changed, exit 0 on change and exit 3 on timeout; meant to be run by Main as a background command so its exit re-invokes Main; bounded, low CPU, tolerant of missing/corrupt state

`stop-hook`: implements the Claude Code Stop hook contract: reads the hook JSON from stdin (session_id, stop_hook_active, ...); only for the authoritative Main session id recorded in the supervisor state (any other session: allow, no output); if actionable items exist that Main has not yet been told about (fingerprint stored in the state directory), print {"decision": "block", "reason": "<one line naming the next item and the command to inspect it>"}; if stop_hook_active is true and the fingerprint is unchanged, allow; at most a configurable number of consecutive blocks (default 3) before allowing; any internal error fails OPEN (allow, exit 0) and is logged to the state directory; reasons never contain secrets or transcript text

`main-settings --out <file> [--python <exe>] [--orchestrator <dir>]`: writes a Claude Code settings JSON containing only a hooks.Stop entry that runs the stop-hook command (argument-safe quoting on Windows), for use with `claude --settings <file>`; it never edits ~/.claude, the repository's .claude/ or any launcher; wiring it into launch.py is a later task (record that as PROPOSED)
